events.title: The Storming of the Bastille
events.description: A crowd of Parisians stormed the Bastille, a royal fortress and prison that symbolized the power of the monarchy. They were searching for gunpowder and weapons, and the fortress fell after a few hours of fighting.
events.significance: The event became the defining symbol of the French Revolution. France still marks July 14 as its national holiday, Bastille Day.

events.title: Billy the Kid Is Killed
events.description: Sheriff Pat Garrett shot and killed the outlaw Billy the Kid at Fort Sumner in New Mexico Territory. Billy had escaped from jail months earlier and had been on the run since.
events.significance: His death ended one of the most famous manhunts of the American Old West. It also helped turn him into a lasting figure of frontier legend.

events.title: Mariner 4 Flies Past Mars
events.description: NASA's Mariner 4 spacecraft made the first successful close flyby of Mars. It sent back the first close-up photographs of another planet, 21 images in all.
events.significance: The images showed a cratered, barren surface. That overturned popular ideas of a more Earth-like Mars and opened a new era of planetary exploration.

events.title: Gerald Ford Is Born
events.description: Gerald R. Ford was born in Omaha, Nebraska, on July 14, 1913. He later served in Congress and became Vice President.
events.significance: Ford became the 38th President of the United States in 1974 after Richard Nixon resigned. He is the only person to hold both the vice presidency and the presidency without being elected to either.
